meta.notes: ECDC's threat-report feed had no item newer than 20 July, and cdc.gov returned HTTP 403 to direct fetches this run; CDC figures come from CDC-attributed reporting instead.

top_stories.label: Top Stories
top_stories.ai_summary: The US shed 23,000 jobs in July when forecasters had penciled in a gain of about 90,000, and markets read the miss as the end of rate-rise pressure — the dollar fell, shares climbed, and the yen jumped far enough that traders started watching for intervention. Washington's other output came from the Senate and the courts: an 86-11 vote for a sweeping Russia and Iran sanctions bill, and another run of rulings against the president, the latest halting his US$400 million White House ballroom. Europe spent the day arguing with itself, as Spain and Italy imposed tit-for-tat border checks over the Ceuta migrant crossings. Asia's news was harder — a school shooting outside Bangkok that killed seven people and the 14-year-old attacker, and floods in Assam that have killed close to 100. The thing to watch: a US official says an Iran-Oman deal to reopen the Strait of Hormuz is now days away.

stories.headline: US payrolls unexpectedly fell by 23,000 in July
stories.summary: The US economy shed 23,000 jobs in July, the Bureau of Labor Statistics reported, against forecasts of a gain of roughly 83,000-95,000. Government employment fell by 53,000, with retail and hospitality also soft. The unemployment rate edged down to 4.1%, but mainly because fewer people were working or looking for work — labour-force participation slid to 61.4%, its lowest in more than five years.
stories.source: CNA, US Bureau of Labor Statistics, CNBC

stories.headline: Dollar slides and stocks rally as weak jobs data eases rate fears
stories.summary: The weak July payrolls print pushed the US dollar lower and equities higher as traders priced in less pressure for further rate increases. The yen surged far enough that CNA reported traders were watching for intervention risk. The move reverses much of the caution that had built up ahead of the release.

stories.headline: Thai PM promises stricter gun laws after school shooting kills eight
stories.summary: Thailand's prime minister said the government would tighten gun laws after a 14-year-old shot dead his grandparents at home and then five staff at Debsirin School in Nonthaburi, near Bangkok, before killing himself — seven victims and the attacker. More than a dozen people were injured; reported injury counts vary between outlets. Police said the handgun belonged to the boy's grandfather. It is Thailand's worst mass shooting since the 2022 Nong Bua Lamphu attack.

stories.headline: Spain imposes border checks on travellers from Italy as Ceuta row escalates
stories.summary: Spain introduced controls on travellers arriving from Italy, retaliating after Rome imposed its own border curbs in the wake of last week's mass crossing into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta. Spanish Foreign Minister Jose Manuel Albares called Italy's restrictions “a torpedo fired at the hull of European unity”; Italy's government replied that it “will not accept ultimatums or impositions”. Spanish authorities are still trying to identify 80 migrants found dead after the Ceuta rush.
stories.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

stories.headline: US Senate passes sweeping Russia and Iran sanctions bill, 86-11
stories.summary: The Senate voted 86-11 for the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026, which targets Russian officials, banks and energy revenues and lets the president impose tariffs of up to 100% on countries that keep buying large volumes of Russian oil and gas. It also widens sanctions on Iran's weapons and energy industries. The bill now goes to the House, where a vote is not expected before early September.
stories.source: The Straits Times, NPR, Washington Post

stories.headline: US official says an Iran-Oman deal on the Strait of Hormuz is expected soon
stories.summary: A US official said Washington expects Iran and Oman to conclude an agreement on the Strait of Hormuz shortly, with commercial shipping to move “without any impediments — meaning no approvals or permissions and no tolls or charges”. Iran has said it wants US and Israeli-linked vessels barred from the strait as part of any accord, a condition Washington has not accepted. Roughly a fifth of the world's seaborne oil and LNG normally passes through the waterway.
stories.source: The Straits Times, Al Jazeera, CNBC

stories.headline: Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan sign a mutual-defence pact
stories.summary: The three governments signed an agreement treating an armed attack on any one of them as an attack on all, after close to a year of negotiations. It gives Gulf states a collective security arrangement outside existing US guarantees at a moment when the Hormuz crisis has exposed their vulnerabilities. Neither Iran nor Israel is named in the text.
stories.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

stories.headline: Germany treats an explosive drone found at Leipzig/Halle airport as a hybrid attack
stories.summary: Germany's federal prosecutor has taken over the investigation into a drone found near a Ukrainian aircraft at Leipzig/Halle, a major NATO and cargo logistics hub, with evidence suggesting it was meant to detonate; a lawmaker said a bus driver kicked it out of the air. Berlin held a security meeting over the incident. Russia's embassy in Berlin dismissed the episode as a “fabricated provocation”, saying accusations were being made without evidence.

stories.headline: US appeals court blocks Trump's US$400 million White House ballroom
stories.summary: A federal appeals court ordered construction of the US$400 million ballroom at the White House halted, blocking a project the president had pushed to build. The ruling is one of a series of court setbacks for the administration; The Straits Times separately reported the administration has now lost 21 consecutive court battles over access to state voter rolls ahead of the November midterms.

stories.headline: Trump's move against 'birth tourism' faces an uphill legal battle
stories.summary: Legal analysts told The Straits Times that the executive orders signed this week to narrow birthright citizenship are unlikely to survive review, given the Supreme Court has already ruled on the question. The orders target children born in the US to parents on short-term visas. Litigation is expected immediately.

stories.headline: Meta ordered to pay US$567 million into a teen mental-health fund
stories.summary: A US state court ordered Meta to pay US$567 million into a fund for teenage mental health, in what the BBC described as the largest child-safety ruling against a social-media company. The award follows litigation over the effects of the company's platforms on young users. Meta is expected to appeal.

stories.headline: World food prices hit a three-year high in July, UN agency says
stories.summary: The UN Food and Agriculture Organization said its food price index reached its highest level in three years in July, with war and El Nino-driven weather pushing costs up and yields down. French farmers are separately bracing for their smallest corn crop since 1980. Import-dependent economies feel this first through cereals and vegetable oils.

stories.headline: Floods in India's north-east kill nearly 100
stories.summary: Flooding in Assam has killed close to 100 people and affected nearly 170,000, with thousands moved into temporary shelters as swollen rivers inundate homes and farmland. Relief operations are continuing across the state.

stories.headline: Houthis strike Marib again as UN warns Yemen is nearing a wider conflict
stories.summary: Yemen's Iran-aligned Houthis fired ballistic missiles and drones at displacement camps and residential areas in Marib, killing two people and wounding 14, according to the state news agency SABA citing local authorities. The figures come from one side of the conflict and have not been independently verified. The UN warned the country is edging towards a broader war.

stories.headline: Zelensky makes a landmark visit to Serbia, a long-standing Russian ally
stories.summary: Ukraine's president travelled to Belgrade for his first visit to Serbia, a country that has kept close ties with Moscow and depends on Russian gas. The Straits Times reported the trip is likely to strain relations between Belgrade and Moscow.

stories.headline: Spanish police arrest 78 in a bust of one of the Mediterranean's largest smuggling networks
stories.summary: Spain said it had dismantled one of the largest human-smuggling networks operating across the Mediterranean, arresting 78 people. The operation comes as Madrid deals with the aftermath of the Ceuta crossings and a diplomatic row with Rome over border controls.

stories.headline: Trump administration to put US$3 billion into critical minerals projects
stories.summary: The president said the federal government would invest US$3 billion across multiple critical-minerals and battery projects, framed as a push to raise domestic production and shore up defence supply chains. It is the latest in a run of industrial-policy interventions.

stories.headline: Russia bans the Navalnaya-chaired Human Rights Foundation as 'undesirable'
stories.summary: Russia designated the New York-based Human Rights Foundation, chaired by Yulia Navalnaya, an “undesirable organisation”, a status that criminalises working with or funding the group inside Russia.

stories.headline: Nurul Izzah takes leave from her PKR deputy president post
stories.summary: Anwar Ibrahim's daughter stepped back from the deputy presidency of Malaysia's Parti Keadilan Rakyat. A source close to her told CNA she had disagreed with the party's direction and faced internal pressure to step down. The move raises questions about the succession picture inside the governing party.

stories.headline: Indonesia's government to take over a state firm's stake in the China-funded Whoosh railway
stories.summary: Jakarta will move the state company's holding in the troubled Jakarta-Bandung high-speed rail into the Danantara fund, CNA reported, as the China-financed project continues to struggle with its debt load. It is the region's first high-speed line and has become a test case for Belt and Road financing.

stories.headline: Indonesia fights a Mount Bromo wildfire as El Nino takes hold
stories.summary: Local authorities deployed two water-bombing helicopters against a fire that has burned at least 127 hectares of national park land at Mount Bromo in East Java. CNA reported the blaze as an early sign of El Nino conditions settling in across the region — the pattern that historically raises fire and haze risk across South-east Asia.

stories.headline: Pacific nations fail to agree a statement condemning China's missile test
stories.summary: Pacific Islands governments could not reach consensus on a joint statement criticising Beijing's intercontinental ballistic missile test last month. CNA reported that China gave only a handful of nations short notice before the launch, with the rocket appearing to come down in ocean somewhere between Solomon Islands, Nauru and Tuvalu.

singapore.label: Singapore
singapore.ai_summary: Two men are to be charged with conspiring to get lawyer Lim Tean out of Singapore illegally, a day after Malaysian police found him in a Johor Bahru apartment — a week-old case that has now opened a second front. The courts did the rest of the heavy lifting, from a former Sakae Holdings director jailed more than 10 years over S$15.8 million to a cash-for-Singpass scheme that ended in three arrests. On policy, the Energy Market Authority cleared solar imports from Malaysia — the thirteenth electricity import project to get the nod — and a public consultation opened on stopping insurers and employers from using people's genetic information. The talk elsewhere is football and farewells, with the Lions through to the ASEAN semi-finals and two long-running dessert names closing. National Day is tomorrow, so expect the rest of the weekend to be fireworks and flypasts.

stories.headline: Two men to be charged over allegedly arranging Lim Tean's illegal exit from Singapore
stories.summary: Two Singaporean men, aged 37 and 44, are to be charged with conspiring to do an act with a tendency to defeat the course of justice, over what police say were arrangements for lawyer Lim Tean to leave Singapore for Malaysia illegally.

stories.headline: Lim Tean arrested in Johor Bahru after failing to surrender for his jail term
stories.summary: Malaysian police arrested the lawyer and opposition politician at an apartment complex in Johor Bahru, days after he did not report to the State Courts to begin serving a sentence for practising law without a valid practising certificate. Singapore police said they are working with the Royal Malaysia Police on his return.

stories.headline: Man to be charged over the death of a petrol station attendant
stories.summary: A man is to be charged with driving without a valid licence and causing the death of a petrol station attendant, and with driving a deregistered vehicle.

stories.headline: Three arrested over a scheme that compromised work permit holders' Singpass accounts
stories.summary: Police arrested three people over an operation that offered work permit holders S$80 in cash in exchange for access to their Singpass accounts. Singpass credentials are the gateway to government and banking services, and handing them over is an offence.

stories.headline: Singapore gives conditional approval to import solar power from Malaysia
stories.summary: The Energy Market Authority granted conditional approvals for solar electricity imports from Malaysia, bringing to 13 the number of electricity import projects that have received conditional approvals or licences. The imports are part of the plan to bring in low-carbon electricity from the region.

stories.headline: Grace Fu says her ministry has no mandate over Maju Forest land-use planning
stories.summary: The Minister for Sustainability and the Environment said MSE does not have the mandate on land-use planning for Maju Forest or Gillman Barracks, following continued public debate over the sites. She had previously addressed the ministry's role in Parliament.

stories.headline: NParks begins sterilising long-tailed macaques at Maju Forest
stories.summary: The National Parks Board said it is sterilising long-tailed macaques at Maju Forest to manage the population, as part of its approach to human-wildlife conflict in the area.

stories.headline: 8kg of cocaine seized from a foreign-registered vessel in Singapore waters
stories.summary: Authorities seized 8kg of cocaine from a foreign-registered commercial vessel in Singapore waters. Investigations are ongoing.

stories.headline: Victims in Singapore, Hong Kong and Macau lose millions in an alleged 'Fun Coffee' Ponzi scheme
stories.summary: Investors across three jurisdictions say they cannot recover their money after the scheme's app went offline on 20 July, leaving them unable to withdraw funds. The Straits Times reported losses running into the millions.

stories.headline: Co-living scheme for young Singaporeans is five times oversubscribed
stories.summary: More than 500 young Singaporeans applied for the co-living rooms on offer, five times the number available. MCCY said most applicants were single youths. It is an early read on demand for rental options aimed at people who cannot yet buy a flat.

stories.headline: Public consultation opens on proposed laws to protect genetic information
stories.summary: The proposed Bill would stop genetic information from being used in insurance and employment decisions. The consultation is open to the public.

stories.headline: Man jailed more than 10 years for misappropriating S$15.8 million from Sakae Holdings
stories.summary: A former director of Sakae Holdings was sentenced to more than 10 years' jail for misappropriating S$15.8 million and for lying in the High Court.

stories.headline: Man jailed for cheating 11 victims of S$3.79 million with fake glove and mask supplies
stories.summary: The man pretended to supply gloves and face masks during the Covid-19 pandemic, cheating 11 victims of S$3.79 million in total.

stories.headline: Jail for a training officer who shoved a woman with an intellectual disability
stories.summary: The former training officer was jailed after pushing a woman with an intellectual disability, causing knee fractures.

stories.headline: Man jailed over 179 upskirt videos and an MRT station molestation
stories.summary: The man took 179 upskirt videos over three years and molested a woman at an MRT station, CNA reported.

stories.headline: Man charged over insulting and profane remarks about the Muslim community on TikTok
stories.summary: A man was charged over remarks made on TikTok that were described in court as insulting and profane towards the Muslim community in Singapore.

stories.headline: Man, 23, charged with trafficking etomidate vape pods
stories.summary: Two vapes and 55 pods were found at his home, according to Mothership; he faces a trafficking charge over etomidate-laced pods. Etomidate is a controlled anaesthetic agent that has been found in vape liquids in Singapore.

stories.headline: Singapore recruits its first nurses from Bhutan
stories.summary: The public healthcare sector has begun taking on nurses from Bhutan to widen its talent pool. Forty graduates of the Asian Nursing Scholarship from Bhutan are already serving in public healthcare here.

stories.headline: Authorities cannot conclude whether any offence was committed in the Indonesian baby-trafficking case
stories.summary: Singapore authorities said they were unable to conclude that an offence was committed here, or by Singapore-based agents, in connection with an Indonesian baby-trafficking ring.

stories.headline: Man dies after a traffic accident in Hougang
stories.summary: A man died following a traffic accident in Hougang, The Straits Times reported. Police investigations are ongoing.

stories.headline: Man nabbed for drug-driving in a three-car Bedok Reservoir Road crash
stories.summary: A man was arrested for driving under the influence of drugs after an accident involving three cars along Bedok Reservoir Road.

stories.headline: Driver who drank gin after a crash to mask his breath alcohol level fined S$8,000
stories.summary: The driver consumed gin after a car accident in an attempt to confuse the reading of his breath alcohol level, and was fined S$8,000.

stories.headline: 5,176 people were arrested for drink-driving in Singapore between 2023 and 2025
stories.summary: Figures cited by Mothership from replies by Home Affairs Minister K. Shanmugam to MP Jamus Lim put drink-driving arrests at 5,176 over the three years to 2025.

stories.headline: CNB investigating the online sale of a Trader Joe's seasoning containing poppy seeds
stories.summary: The Central Narcotics Bureau said it is looking into online sales of a Trader Joe's seasoning product containing poppy seeds, which are prohibited in Singapore, and will take the necessary action.

stories.headline: Dead fish at Sungei Buloh were likely trapped and killed by the recent hot weather, NParks says
stories.summary: NParks said fish found dead at Sungei Buloh were most likely trapped in shallow water and died as a result of the recent hot weather, rather than from pollution or mistreatment.

stories.headline: Director behind firms in the unpaid workers case files for bankruptcy
stories.summary: The director of the companies at the centre of the unpaid workers case has filed for bankruptcy, The Straits Times reported.

stories.headline: Missing woman, 42, last seen in Ang Mo Kio
stories.summary: Police appealed for information on a 42-year-old woman last seen in Ang Mo Kio.

stories.headline: Man given a police award for helping arrest a suspected thief on a flight to Singapore
stories.summary: The Singapore Police Force gave the man an award for assisting in the arrest of a suspected thief aboard a flight to Singapore. The suspect is set to be charged with theft on 8 August.

stories.headline: Worker fined S$8,000 for dumping 1,530kg of waste at a Tampines heavy vehicle park
stories.summary: A worker was fined S$8,000 after dumping 1,530kg of household and renovation waste at a heavy vehicle park in Tampines.

stories.headline: Singapore reach the ASEAN championship semi-finals after drawing with Indonesia
stories.summary: A draw against Indonesia was enough to take the Lions through to the semi-finals of the ASEAN football championship. Coach Gavin Lee said afterwards that “nobody gave us a chance in this group”.

stories.headline: Two National Day films spark an 'AI slop' debate
stories.summary: Two Singapore films set for release around National Day have drawn argument over their use of generative AI, with critics calling the results “AI slop” and the makers defending the approach. The row lands days before the SG61 celebrations.

stories.headline: Kit Chan's 'Home' gets a first-ever vinyl release, pressed in the shape of Singapore
stories.summary: The original recording of the National Day standard is being pressed to vinyl for the first time, on a record cut into the outline of the island.

stories.headline: Two long-running dessert names are closing: Pantler and Laurent Cafe & Chocolate Bar
stories.summary: Japanese-French patisserie Pantler will shut after 12 years unless a buyer takes it over, with The Straits Times reporting a closing date of 30 August. Separately, Laurent Cafe & Chocolate Bar at Robertson Quay is closing after 20 years.

stories.headline: Man filmed washing his motorcycle inside a Kent Ridge Park toilet
stories.summary: Footage of a man washing a motorcycle inside a public toilet at Kent Ridge Park circulated online, and NParks said it is investigating.

stories.headline: Software engineer quits a S$10,000-a-month job to sell hokkien mee
stories.summary: A Singaporean left a S$10,000 software engineering salary to run a hokkien mee stall and now earns about a third of what he did before, Mothership reported.

stories.headline: Man fined S$3,000 after refusing to pay for porridge and harassing police at Orchard Plaza
stories.summary: A 36-year-old man was fined S$3,000 after getting drunk, refusing to pay for porridge at Orchard Plaza and then harassing the police officers who responded.

stories.headline: River Wonders debuts a red panda and a new exhibit for the National Day weekend
stories.summary: The river-themed zoo will house a red panda for the first time in 12 years, with the new exhibit opening over the National Day weekend.

stories.headline: A giant map of Singapore built from 28,000 bottle caps
stories.summary: Volunteers and residents in Sengkang East recreated Singapore's landmarks using 28,000 bottle caps and satay sticks.

stories.headline: Nerf bullets, a slipper and underwear among the litter jamming reverse vending machines
stories.summary: Operators of the beverage container return scheme found a Nerf gun bullet, a slipper and underwear among items stuffed into machines meant for recyclable bottles and cans. The interface has been tweaked to cut down on failed refunds.

stories.headline: Where to watch the NDP 2026 fireworks
stories.summary: The Straits Times listed six vantage points for the National Day fireworks, with the main display expected at about 8.15pm on 9 August.

stories.headline: She quit school twice; now her horror art studio's neon art jams book out most weekends
stories.summary: CNA profiled Merida Lim, whose horror-themed art studio Scuro nearly closed before its neon art-jamming sessions began selling out most weekends.

wars.label: Wars & Conflicts
wars.ai_summary: The Hormuz standoff is closer to a settlement than at any point since February: a US official now expects Iran and Oman to conclude a shipping arrangement within days, though Tehran's demand to bar US and Israeli vessels is not something Washington has accepted. What shifted around it is the security architecture, with the Saudi-Turkiye-Pakistan mutual-defence pact giving Gulf states a collective answer that does not run through Washington — that matters more for the next crisis than this one. Yemen is the piece moving the wrong way, as Houthi missiles hit camps in Marib and the UN warns of a wider war. On the Russian front the pressure has turned financial and forensic rather than territorial, the Senate sanctions vote landing the same week Germany opened a sabotage inquiry at a NATO logistics airport. Lebanon is unusually the quiet one: the short-list of countries to verify Hezbollah's disarmament is the first concrete step there, and the one to watch if the wider roadmap is to hold.

theatres.name: Russia–Ukraine War
theatres.status: Sanctions pressure stepping up in Washington while Europe treats sabotage on its own soil as part of the war; both sides still trading long-range strikes

timeline.event: Russia launches its full-scale invasion of Ukraine. The war is now in its fifth year.
After a deadly strike on Kyiv, Ukraine warns that its shortage of air-defence interceptors is costing lives. Patriot stocks are stretched worldwide.
Ukraine hits two oil refineries deep inside Russian territory; BBC News reports from Odesa on a new pattern of Russian Black Sea strikes on the port city.
The Straits Times reports from Moscow that Ukraine's strikes on the e-commerce operator Wildberries are squeezing ordinary Russian businesses that depend on its pick-up network.
Russia designates the New York-based Human Rights Foundation, chaired by Yulia Navalnaya, an 'undesirable organisation'.
A Russia-linked group is blamed for circulating a fake video showing German Chancellor Friedrich Merz resigning.

The US Senate votes 86-11 to pass a sanctions bill targeting Russian officials, banks and energy revenues, and authorising tariffs of up to 100% on major buyers of Russian oil and gas. The House is not expected to vote before September.
timeline.source: The Straits Times, NPR, Washington Post

timeline.event: Germany's federal prosecutor takes over the investigation into an explosive drone found near a Ukrainian aircraft at Leipzig/Halle airport, a NATO logistics hub, and Berlin holds a security meeting. Russia's embassy calls the incident a 'fabricated provocation'.
Zelensky makes his first visit to Serbia, a long-standing Russian ally and gas customer.

theatres.name: US/Israel–Iran (Strait of Hormuz)
theatres.status: Closest to a shipping deal since the strait closed — US officials expect an Iran-Oman agreement within days — but Yemen is deteriorating and Iran's terms are still contested

timeline.event: The United States and Israel attack Iran. Tehran responds by largely closing the Strait of Hormuz, through which about a fifth of the world's seaborne oil and LNG normally passes.
President Trump says he has cancelled planned strikes on Iran, conditional on a deal being made 'rapidly'.
Iran and Oman say talks on reopening the strait are in their final stages; the framework would route inbound commercial traffic through an Iranian-controlled lane and outbound through an Omani one.
Iran says it wants US and Israeli ships barred from the strait as part of any peace accord — a condition Washington has not accepted.
Israel dismisses senior intelligence officials, with reporting attributing the shake-up to an expanding Iranian spy network.
Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan sign a mutual-defence pact treating an armed attack on one as an attack on all, after nearly a year of talks.
timeline.source: BBC News, CNA, The Straits Times

timeline.event: A US official says a deal between Iran and Oman is expected soon, with any temporary routes to carry 'no approvals or permissions and no tolls or charges'. Iraq's prime minister and Saudi Arabia's intelligence chief separately discuss regional security as Iraqi militias hold off on a response.

Houthi missiles and drones hit displacement camps and residential areas in Marib, killing two and wounding 14 according to Yemen's SABA agency citing local authorities — a claim from one party to the conflict, not independently verified. The UN warns Yemen is nearing a wider conflict.

theatres.name: Israel–Gaza & Lebanon
theatres.status: Verification machinery for Hezbollah's disarmament is being assembled, but Israel's governing coalition is fraying over the draft law

timeline.event: BBC News sets out the Gaza peace-deal roadmap after Hamas signals acceptance of a disarmament framework; Israeli politicians voice scepticism.
At least 13 people are killed in Israeli strikes on Gaza after Hamas agreed the disarmament deal, Palestinian authorities say. Israel has said it will not withdraw ahead of full disarmament.
Israel strikes southern Lebanon after two of its soldiers are killed by an explosion, testing the ceasefire.
Israel charges a settler over the killing of a Palestinian who was involved in an Oscar-winning film about the West Bank.

The Straits Times reports widening faultlines in Prime Minister Netanyahu's coalition, with far-right ally Bezalel Smotrich under pressure and a breakaway party courting his voters over the military draft impasse.
Lebanon and Israel agree a short-list of countries that could send troops to verify Hezbollah's disarmament. An official declined to name any of them.

outbreaks.label: Outbreaks
outbreaks.ai_summary: DR Congo's Ebola epidemic has crossed a line that national reporting now puts above WHO's last formal count, and it is already the largest the country has ever recorded — the trajectory, not the total, is the worrying part. A scare on a river boat near Kinshasa ended in seven negative tests, so it stays concentrated in the east rather than reaching the capital. The other two active pictures are domestic to the US: measles is having its worst year since 1991, and a jalapeno-linked Salmonella outbreak is still being traced through Mexican suppliers. Nothing here is spreading in South-east Asia, but anyone travelling to eastern DR Congo is worth a vaccination check.

outbreaks.name: Ebola (Bundibugyo virus) — DR Congo, Uganda, France
outbreaks.status: Largest Ebola outbreak ever recorded in DR Congo and still expanding; national reporting has now passed 4,000 confirmed cases
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO-confirmed cases only, as of 30 July 2026, from Disease Outbreak News 614 published 1 August: DR Congo 3,605 confirmed cases with 1,587 deaths (CFR 44%), Uganda 20 with 2 deaths, France 1. Two DR Congo patients were also treated in Germany. The outbreak is active in 33 of 49 affected health zones, with Ituri province accounting for 88% of cases. On 7 August, Congolese government data carried by The Straits Times put DR Congo above 4,000 confirmed cases — a figure newer than, and not yet ratified in, a WHO DON.

outbreaks.name: Measles — United States
outbreaks.status: Highest US case count since 1991; no deaths so far this year; 94% of cases outbreak-associated
outbreaks.scope_note: US CDC surveillance data as of 6 August 2026: 2,465 confirmed cases in 2026, of which 2,449 were reported by 47 jurisdictions and 16 among international visitors; 38 separate outbreaks, with 2,309 of the 2,465 cases (94%) outbreak-associated. CDC reports 93% of infected people were unvaccinated, and no measles deaths have been recorded in the US in 2026 (three were recorded in 2025). This is the highest annual US total since 1991. cdc.gov returned HTTP 403 to direct fetch attempts this run, so these figures come from CDC-attributed reporting rather than a page read directly.

outbreaks.name: Salmonella Javiana — United States (jalapenos)
outbreaks.status: Traced to jalapenos from Sinaloa, Mexico; recalled product pulled by restaurant chains
outbreaks.scope_note: CDC/FDA outbreak tally: 345 illnesses across 27 states, 36 hospitalisations and no deaths, with illness onsets from 19 June to 20 July 2026. Of 191 people interviewed, 177 (93%) had eaten at a Mexican-style restaurant, including Chipotle and QDOBA. Traceback points to fresh jalapenos grown in Sinaloa, Mexico and distributed by Coast Citrus Distributors; two isolates showed antibiotic resistance. CDC notes the true case count is likely higher.

outbreaks.name: Andes hantavirus — MV Hondius cruise cluster
outbreaks.status: Ship cluster closed out and figures now more than five weeks old; a separate, unlinked European case surfaced this week
outbreaks.scope_note: WHO DON611 figures as of 2 July 2026: 13 cases (12 confirmed, one probable) including three deaths (two confirmed, one probable), all among people who travelled on the M/V Hondius; case fatality ratio 23%. WHO has not issued an update since, so these numbers are stale. 'Countries' is not a single figure — cases were reported across several countries plus Tristan da Cunha. Separately, France's hantavirus reference centre confirmed an Andes-strain infection this week in a Franco-Argentine traveller who was in France in late July and is now isolated in Spain; officials have found no link to the ship cluster, so that case is not counted here.

stories.headline: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak passes 4,000 confirmed cases
stories.summary: Government data showed confirmed cases in the Democratic Republic of the Congo rising above 4,000 for the first time in this outbreak. WHO's most recent Disease Outbreak News, published 1 August with data to 30 July, had the DR Congo count at 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths; the 4,000 figure is national reporting and has not yet been ratified in a WHO DON.

stories.headline: Seven passengers on a river boat intercepted near Kinshasa test negative for Ebola
stories.summary: Congolese health authorities said seven passengers on a boat stopped near Kinshasa tested negative, easing fears the virus had spread on board after a passenger suspected of having the disease died. Kinshasa is far from the outbreak's centre in Ituri province, so any confirmed case there would have marked a significant geographic jump.

stories.headline: A new Andes hantavirus case is confirmed in a traveller, unlinked to the cruise-ship cluster
stories.summary: France's national hantavirus reference centre confirmed an Andes-strain infection in a Franco-Argentine traveller who developed mild respiratory symptoms in France in the second half of July and later moved to Spain, where they are isolated and asymptomatic. Officials say they have found no link to the MV Hondius cluster and are working through the patient's travel history and contacts.

stories.headline: US measles cases reach a 35-year high at 2,465 confirmed
stories.summary: CDC surveillance updated on 6 August put confirmed US measles cases for 2026 at 2,465 — the highest annual total since 1991 — across 38 separate outbreaks. No measles deaths have been recorded in the US this year; three were recorded in 2025. Ninety-four per cent of cases are outbreak-associated and CDC says 93% of those infected were unvaccinated, which puts the country's measles elimination status at risk.

cybersecurity.label: CyberSecurity
cybersecurity.ai_summary: Patch Metabase first: an unauthenticated SQL-injection zero-day rated CVSS 10.0 was used to steal customer data from Framework, Tally and LexisNexis before any fix existed, and self-hosted instances stay exposed until someone updates them by hand. WordPress is the other one to do today — every version carried a pre-auth login cross-site scripting flaw that chains to PHP execution on the server, fixed in 7.0.3. After that it is the usual edge-and-infrastructure queue, led by three Cisco SD-WAN flaws scoring 9.9 and a KEV-listed TeamCity bug that hands an attacker a build server's signing keys. The software supply chain had its worst week in a while, with nearly 800 malicious npm packages shipping a cross-platform remote access trojan. And the AI-tooling flaws have stopped being theoretical: a GitHub issue can now reach CI secrets through a coding agent — our own tooling included.

stories.headline: Metabase SQL-injection zero-day exploited to steal customer data
stories.summary: An unauthenticated SQL injection flaw in Metabase 1.58 and above lets attackers inject arbitrary SQL into the application database and take administrator control of an instance. It was exploited as a zero-day: laptop maker Framework had customer names, emails, addresses, phone numbers and billing details stolen, form builder Tally lost email addresses and password hashes on 3 August, and LexisNexis said its Metabase API was affected. No CVE has been assigned yet. Fixes are out in 0.58.24, 0.59.21, 0.60.17, 0.61.11, 0.62.9 and 0.63.5; cloud instances are patched, self-hosted ones are not. Blocking /api/session/reset_password is the stopgap.

stories.headline: Unlimited Technology Systems breach affects 3.8 million people
stories.summary: The physical-security and technology services firm disclosed a breach affecting 3.8 million people. BleepingComputer reported the disclosure; the categories of data involved are set out in the company's notification.

stories.headline: Nearly 800 malicious npm packages deliver a cross-platform RAT and infostealer
stories.summary: Researchers found close to 800 packages published to npm that install a remote access trojan and infostealer working across Windows, macOS and Linux. It is the largest wave in a run of npm campaigns over the past fortnight. Audit lockfiles and recently added transitive dependencies rather than only direct ones.

stories.headline: ClickFix lures deliver a macOS stealer that drains crypto wallets
stories.summary: Fake verification prompts trick macOS users into pasting a command into Terminal, installing an infostealer built to empty cryptocurrency wallets. Over 250 ClickFix domains using browser fingerprinting to hide the macOS lure from researchers were catalogued in the same week.

stories.headline: UNC6671 calls staff on their personal phones to talk them out of SaaS data
stories.summary: The extortion group, linked to BlackFile, is placing voice-phishing calls to employees' personal mobile numbers rather than work lines, sidestepping corporate call controls to obtain access to SaaS platforms. BleepingComputer tied a run of hedge-fund intrusions to the same group. Awareness training that only covers work channels misses this.

stories.headline: North Carolina Ports confirms a cyberattack disrupting operations
stories.summary: The port authority confirmed a cyberattack that disrupted operations. Port and logistics operators have been a recurring target this year, and disruption there propagates into freight schedules well beyond the operator itself.

stories.headline: WordPress patches a pre-auth login XSS that can be chained to PHP execution
stories.summary: XSS2Shell is a reflected cross-site scripting flaw on the WordPress login screen that affects every version of the CMS: a crafted username reaching the failed-login error page runs attacker JavaScript in the site's origin with no authentication. Chained with a logged-in administrator clicking an attacker-controlled page, and under specific deployment conditions, it reaches PHP code execution on the server. Fixed in WordPress 7.0.3 on 6 August, backported through the 4.7 branch. No in-the-wild exploitation reported yet — patch before that changes.

stories.headline: SCTPhantom: an 18-year-old Linux SCTP flaw gives local root and container escape
stories.summary: A use-after-free in the kernel's SCTP handling, present for 18 years, lets a local user gain root and break out of a container. NVD has the CVE without a published CVSS score. Distribution kernel updates are the fix; disabling the SCTP module is the mitigation where it is not needed.

stories.headline: NatJack attacks hijack TCP sessions and spoof DNS by manipulating NAT tables
stories.summary: An origin-validation error in Windows Network Address Translation lets an unauthorised attacker manipulate NAT state to hijack TCP sessions and spoof DNS responses. A second identifier, CVE-2026-63913, covers the related issue in other implementations.

stories.headline: Microsoft 365 adversary-in-the-middle phishing harvests payroll and finance email
stories.summary: An AitM phishing campaign is taking over Microsoft 365 accounts and then quietly collecting payroll and finance correspondence — the reconnaissance step for payment-diversion fraud. Session-token theft defeats standard MFA; phishing-resistant authenticators and conditional-access policies are the mitigations.

stories.headline: AI-assisted research finds new HTTP desync techniques and an Apache Traffic Server zero-day
stories.summary: An AI-driven fuzzing harness turned up previously unknown HTTP request-smuggling techniques along with a zero-day in Apache Traffic Server. Desync bugs let an attacker poison a shared front-end connection and reach other users' requests, which makes them worth prioritising on any reverse-proxy tier.

stories.headline: Malware can abuse Windows Hello for Business keys for persistent Entra ID access
stories.summary: Malware already running on a device can register or reuse Windows Hello for Business keys to keep signing in to Entra ID, surviving password resets. Detection means watching for unexpected WHfB key registrations rather than relying on credential rotation.

stories.headline: Claude Code and Gemini CLI flaws let a GitHub issue reach CI workflow secrets
stories.summary: Improper neutralisation in the Gemini CLI container launcher (CVE-2026-12537, CVSS 10.0) lets content in a GitHub issue reach OS commands inside a CI workflow and read its secrets. A separate, lower-severity Claude Code issue (CVE-2026-54316, CVSS 6.0, fixed in 2.1.163) allowed a pre-trusted hostname to be abused. Anything that pipes untrusted repository content into an agent running with CI credentials needs the same review — including our own tooling.

stories.headline: Swiss government SharePoint breach compromised 200 accounts
stories.summary: A SharePoint compromise in Swiss federal systems affected around 200 accounts. SharePoint on-premises has been one of the most heavily exploited enterprise targets this year.

stories.headline: TONTOU interrupt-injection attack bypasses Spectre v2 defences on Intel and AMD
stories.summary: A new interrupt-injection technique defeats existing Spectre v2 mitigations on both Intel and AMD processors and was demonstrated leaking Linux password hashes. As with earlier speculative-execution work, the practical exposure is highest on shared and multi-tenant hosts.

stories.headline: Zapscape KVM flaw lets privileged L1 guest code escape to the Linux host
stories.summary: A KVM issue in the Linux kernel's x86 root-handling lets privileged code inside a nested guest break out to the host. NVD lists the CVE without a published CVSS score. Hypervisor escapes matter most to anyone running untrusted or customer-controlled VMs.

stories.headline: Cisco patches 12 SD-WAN and IOS XE flaws, three of them scoring 9.9
stories.summary: Cisco's release covers 12 vulnerabilities in Catalyst SD-WAN and IOS XE, three rated CVSS 9.9 (CVE-2026-20303, CVE-2026-20304 and CVE-2026-20310, with CVE-2026-20272 also addressed). Edge routers sit at the network boundary, so these belong at the front of the patch queue.

stories.headline: Weak randomness in CryptoJS is behind US$5.7 million in wallet drains
stories.summary: A weak random number generator in CryptoJS produced predictable keys in five cryptocurrency wallet applications, and researchers attribute about US$5.7 million in drained funds to it. Any key material generated by an affected build has to be treated as compromised and rotated — patching alone does not help.

stories.headline: Apple iCloud Private Relay can expose real IP addresses through WebKit proxy bypasses
stories.summary: Certain WebKit code paths route around iCloud Private Relay, revealing a user's real IP address to a site that is supposed to see only the relay. It undercuts the privacy guarantee the feature is bought for.

stories.headline: Attackers compile the khunt toolkit inside Oracle to turn SQL injection into SYSTEM access
stories.summary: Intruders are using Oracle's own facilities to compile and run the khunt post-exploitation toolkit from inside the database, escalating a SQL injection into Windows SYSTEM privileges on the host. Database servers that are not monitored as endpoints give this a long dwell time.

stories.headline: CoreBreak: AWS, Google and Vercel agent flaws let attackers trigger tools without the model
stories.summary: Flaws in agent frameworks from AWS, Google and Vercel let an attacker invoke tools directly, skipping the model that is supposed to authorise them — so guardrails implemented at the prompt layer never run. Tracked as CVE-2026-18236, CVE-2026-18830, CVE-2026-64650 and CVE-2026-64651; all three vendors have shipped fixes.

stories.headline: Chinese-made Zbtlink routers ship with a backdoor opening unauthenticated root shells
stories.summary: Zbtlink routers were found shipping with an undocumented service that hands out root shells without authentication. There is no fix for an implanted backdoor short of replacing or reflashing the device; treat affected units as untrusted.

stories.headline: CISA adds an actively exploited JetBrains TeamCity RCE to its KEV catalog
stories.summary: Unauthenticated remote code execution in JetBrains TeamCity before 2026.1.3 and 2025.11.7 is being exploited in the wild; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 5 August. A build server holds signing keys and deployment credentials, which makes this a supply-chain problem as much as a server one.
stories.source: The Hacker News, CISA KEV, NVD

stories.headline: CISA flags Langflow, Apache Tomcat and N-able N-central flaws as actively exploited
stories.summary: CISA added IBM Langflow code injection (CVE-2026-9198), Apache Tomcat missing encryption of sensitive data (CVE-2026-34486) and two N-able N-central authentication bypasses (CVE-2026-18556 and CVE-2026-18577) to the KEV catalog on 3-4 August, after customer compromises via N-central. Federal agencies face binding remediation deadlines; everyone else should treat KEV listing as the exploitation signal it is.
stories.source: BleepingComputer, The Hacker News, CISA KEV

stories.headline: Veeam, Terraform MCP and Django patch critical flaws, led by a CVSS 10.0 cross-tenant bug
stories.summary: The worst of the batch is a cross-tenant credential-reuse flaw in terraform-mcp-server before 1.1.0 (CVE-2026-16498, CVSS 10.0) that lets one tenant reuse another's credentials. Veeam (CVE-2026-58073) and Django (CVE-2026-15307) shipped critical fixes in the same window.

stories.headline: Critical Gitea flaw let unauthenticated attackers read server files via Org-mode markup
stories.summary: A flaw in Gitea's Org-mode markup rendering allowed unauthenticated attackers to read files from the server. The vendor rates it critical; NVD has no published record for the identifier yet, so no CVSS score is given here. Self-hosted Gitea instances exposed to the internet should be updated.
